expectation: Membrane ring on scattered single myeloid cells (macrophages, neutrophils, monocytes) in the gut lamina propria between crypts and in the submucosa; moderately common, absent from the epithelium; neutrophils may cluster in inflamed foci.
observed: A: yellow haze over all tissue, and bright dots both on and off the tissue. B, C: diffuse haze plus a few irregular bright blobs, no membrane rings. D: fuzzy blobs with no cell outline. E: CD66b is plain haze, so row E tells nothing.
why: The signal is tissue-wide haze plus debris-like blobs that also appear off the tissue; there is no distinct population of ringed myeloid cells in the lamina propria.
notes: CD11b shows haze that follows the tissue and bright speckles that also sit on bare slide. The few bright spots in B to D are irregular blobs, not membrane-stained cells. The partner CD66b has no cell structure, so the co-expression row can't help.
